it appeared as the Golden World, cleared and serene.
Immediately, as many Buddhas, Tathāgatas, as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of billions of Buddha-fields appeared simultaneously to act as witnesses,
all together praising Mañjuśrī as the foremost leader.
Together with the sixteen great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, such as Samantabhadra,
I vow that all sentient beings may swiftly cultivate and realize [this].
One will swiftly attain the realization of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, all Tathāgatas will appear, offer praise, and act as witnesses.
All the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, spoke with one voice in unison:
"Mañjuśrī shall be the foremost among the bodhisattvas, together with Samantabhadra,
the sixteen great beings, and the rest."
They received the proclamation and praise of the Buddhas for their profound practice and virtue:
"Excellent, excellent, Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, and the sixteen great Bodhisattvas!
You have been able, since the time of your causal stages in the past, throughout immeasurable kalpas..."
They give rise to vast and great vows to deliver sentient beings;
their minds are equal to space and never cease.
This is the practice of the sixteen Great Beings as they cultivate the bodhisattva path.
The merit is profoundly deep and inexhaustible;
the Tathāgata bears witness that it is immeasurable and beyond comparison.
These supreme vows are unspeakably unspeakable and inconceivable.
When the Tathāgata had finished speaking,
six great Vajras suddenly appeared;
they too, with one voice, praised the profound and virtuous conduct of the sixteen great Bodhisattvas, Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra, acting as witnesses.
The Vajrapāṇi said:
"Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, and others are unspeakable in number;
they have all attained unimpeded eloquence."
Realizing the great Dharma-patience and accomplishing Bodhi,
they subjugate Māra and his enmity, restrain all heterodox paths,
and reach the stage of the Tathāgata’s noble nature and vajra-wisdom.
In this one lifetime, they shall attain the vajra-like holy power of dhāraṇī,
true fearlessness, and sovereign supernormal powers;
they shall realize the Tathāgata’s Dharma-body, all its merits, and the ground of all Buddhas.
They are fully endowed with inexhaustible great wisdom, which is inconceivable and cannot be fully described.
What is their protection? How is it that they are called the six great *māhārājika* *vajra*-protectors who assist and guard the Buddha-dharma?
First is Mahāsukha, second is Mahāhāsa,
third is Ekajaṭī, fourth is Trailokyavijaya,
fifth is Caturmukha, and sixth is Yamāntaka-Ṣaṇmukha.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Siṃhavikrama:
"You should, with profound faith, [hear] these six great Vajra-wielders proclaiming in unison:
'We, the six great Vajras, have made this great vow.'"
Furthermore, we shall together follow the past conduct and vows of Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra;
we shall uphold the instructions of the Tathāgata and constantly protect the Buddha-dharma,
ensuring that it is not disturbed or agitated by celestial Māras or various evil non-Buddhists.
I vow that until the end of the future,
my mind shall always protect and sustain all things equal to the Dharma-realm,
so that all sentient beings may fulfill their vows, attain Bodhi, and achieve the Unsurpassed Way.
At that time, within that great assembly among the host of bodhisattvas,
the Bodhisattva Siṃhavikrāntagāminigarjitasvara rose from his seat,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"From what place have the Tathāgatas, as numerous as atoms,
whom I have previously mentioned, come to serve as witnesses?
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Siṃhavikrāmin:
Thus, these sixteen great beings,
such as Mañjuśrī and the others, while on the path of practice in the past,
instructed sentient beings and caused them to resolve upon the Mahāyāna *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
They shall attain Buddhahood early and shall likewise manifest as all Buddhas, as numerous as motes of dust;
this is due to causes from the past.
Therefore, Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, and the sixteen bodhisattvas shall act as witnesses.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Siṃhavikrama was present among the great assembly.
With earnest prostrations, he addressed the World-Honored One,
saying: "In the distant past, long ago, when I was still on the path as a bodhisattva,
I once accompanied the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī."
In the world-system Kāṣāyadhvaja,
there is a Buddha named Kāṣāyaratnadhvaja Tathāgata,
with whom he together with the bodhisattvas likewise went forth as a renunciant among the śrāvakas.
"Why is it that now we have obtained the appearance of Buddhas as numerous as atoms to come and provide witness?
This great assembly of ours truly finds this difficult to believe.
At that time, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni addressed them, saying:
Then, for the great assembly of many bodhisattva-mahāsattvas such as Siṃhavikrama and others,
he expounded the causes and conditions of Mañjuśrī’s past lives under former buddhas during his stage of practice.
It proves the attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
and it also states that Mañjuśrī has long ago resided in a Buddha-world acting as a Mahāyāna bodhisattva.
Long ago, they gave rise to the unsurpassed mind of bodhicitta and practiced and studied progressively through immeasurable kalpas.
At that time, during the appearance of the Tathāgata Ratnaketu in the world, they...
Having left the household life among the assembly of śrāvakas to become a śramaṇa,
he employs skillful means to guide and lead the assembly of śrāvakas,
causing them to resolve upon the mind of unsurpassed bodhi.
One should take refuge in the Mahāyāna and gradually cultivate it through successive stages.
One’s mind shall be vast and expansive, equal to space.
Mañjuśrī, the Great Being, will sincerely guide and lead one.
Furthermore, I make this great vow before the numinous spirits and divine beings of the dark realms:
may you bear witness to me and cause my vows to be fulfilled for the sake of all sentient beings.
Having gradually trained in the vajra-bodhi of the Tathāgata’s noble nature,
the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī subsequently practiced through countless *bhadra-kalpas* across Buddha-fields, life after life.
It was during a kalpa of this Buddha-field named Pure Radiance (Vimalaprabhā).
At that time, the world was called Merudhvaja;
although within that world there were various mountains and the impure, evil beings of the five destinies dwelling together in confusion.
Nevertheless, that land is composed of various jewels;
it is pure, magnificently adorned, and free from all impurities and evils.
It contains ten billion sets of four continents and ten billion worlds.
Within it, there was a Buddha-field world consisting of four continents,
named Siṃhagarbha World. In that world,
there were eight billion royal cities.
Within those eight billion royal cities,
there was one royal city named Sovereign Banner City (*Svayambhūdhvaja*).
In that city, there was a wheel-turning sage king (*cakravartin rājan*).

The Tathāgata, having thus expounded the ten great compassionate contemplations of the Vajra and the dhāraṇī,
at that time the World-Honored One [reiterated] as previously stated the teachings of the Buddhas regarding the ten great compassionate contemplations and the recitation of the dhāraṇī.
The Tathāgata fully expounded the sublime, holy power and merit of sustaining the Saṅgha,
so that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and all sentient beings may cultivate and enter [this path] and swiftly realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of all Buddhas.
Therefore, Siṃhavikrama and all bodhisattvas,
we shall with deep faith vow to uphold [this].
What are the names of the ten great beings, the bodhisattvas of superior intent, and so forth, from the ten directions?
Having likewise attained the Dharma teachings authorized by the Tathāgata and practicing the Bodhisattva path,
they each stood before the World-Honored One in the presence of the great assembly,
together with the multitude of bodhisattvas.
He himself spoke of the secret contemplative gateways of the teachings on cultivation and realization;
furthermore, in the future, he shall likewise save and deliver all sentient beings together with all bodhisattvas.
Therefore, what is called the "Contemplation of the Ten Great Beings of this Secret Vajra"?
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni sequentially taught the ten great beings,
the mahāsattvas such as the Bodhisattva Upariṣṭāśaya from the upper direction.
The World-Honored One commanded ten great beings, bodhisattvas,
each to personally expound upon their gateways of contemplation.
The first was the Great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Bodhisattva, Superior Intention, from the World of Sublime Joy and Delight in the Upper Direction.
One should personally declare this before the Tathāgata,
so that all bodhisattvas of the future may cultivate entry into the noble nature and noble wisdom of bodhi.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva of Superior Intent, who has realized the samādhi of the Tathāgata’s three vajra secrets and perceives his own nature,
enters the contemplation of the immovable nirvāṇa of non-substantiality.
Then he enters the samādhi of the sovereign dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas.
With the eye of his own noble wisdom,
the Bodhisattva contemplates the sphere of the mental consciousness and enters this samādhi of the diamond-like dharma-realm, which is the contemplation of nirvāṇa as being without intrinsic nature.
The Bodhisattva Shangyi perceives within his own body the nature-born mind-made body (*manomayakāya*).
Within each and every pore,
he exercises mastery over the supernatural powers of entry and exit through his holy strength.
He attained the profound realization of the samādhi of the inconceivable dharma-realm.
By means of the wisdom of his noble nature, he knew all the Buddha-dharmas of the three periods of time—both those that can be expressed and those that cannot be expressed.
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field practice,
instruct, and transform all sentient beings;
they perform the deeds of a bodhisattva constantly without rest, [aiming] for all sentient beings.
Swiftly enter nirvāṇa through the contemplation of the naturelessness [of phenomena], and through the noble power of the dharma-realm, attain the siddhi of bodhi;
become a perfected bodhisattva and cause all sentient beings to first practice and realize this.
Enter the contemplation of the ten kinds of great dharmas of the three secrets of the adamantine bodhi that achieve perfection.
What are called the ten kinds of great dharmas of the three secrets of adamantine bodhi?
First, it enables one to realize and enter the light of the secret dharmas of a hundred thousand dharanis,
and to accomplish the great dharma of the practice of the three mysteries of the bodhi-vajra-sattva nature.
Second, it enables one to realize and enter hundreds of thousands of faculties and wisdoms that perfectly accomplish the spiritual powers of enlightenment,
and to realize and enter hundreds of thousands of samādhis, the great dharmas of the Buddha-samādhis.
Third, it is the Great Dharma because it enables one to realize and enter hundreds of thousands of spiritual powers (*ṛddhi*),
accomplishes and nurtures hundreds of thousands of Vajra-samayas,
and brings to perfection the noble power of enlightenment.
Fourth, it enables one to realize and enter hundreds of thousands of gateways to emptiness;
to enter the stage of the noble ground of samādhi of all Tathāgatas; to achieve the movement toward bodhi;
and to travel freely through the ten directions by means of sovereign supernormal powers.
Fifth, they are able to cause one to realize and enter the gateways of samādhi of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas;
their noble nature is thoroughly penetrated, and they fully accomplish bodhi.
The sublime and secret gates of the various *pāramitās*;
the great Dharma that is the unimpeded perfection of the wisdom of awakening (*bodhi*) regarding the nature of all things;
and sixth, the ability to cause one to realize and enter hundreds of thousands of noble wisdoms and supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
By cultivating entry into the essential nature of the principles of sublime conduct, one accumulates merit, accomplishes the noble path, and realizes awakening.
One enters the great Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas.

Seventh, it enables the realization and entry into hundreds of thousands of eloquences, wisdoms, and skillful means for the purpose of expounding the accomplishment of the Tathāgata’s noble conduct and awakening.
It is the great Dharma that deeply penetrates the secret meaning of all phenomena.
Eighth, it enables one to realize and enter the profound and great compassionate noble practices of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas,
and to accomplish the great Dharma of the perfect conduct of a Buddha leading to enlightenment.
Ninth, it enables one to realize and enter the path of the vajra-nature of the Tathāgata’s hundreds of thousands of noble wisdoms,
to receive the Buddha’s consecration, to enter the rank of the Dharma King, and to achieve awakening.
The Great Illumination of the Wisdom-Body of all Buddhas, the Vajra Bodhi,
accomplishes the Dharma-body and brings about the Great Dharma of liberation.
Tenth, it enables one to realize and enter the stage of liberation of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, to accomplish Bodhi, and to attain all Tathāgatas.
Swiftly enter the samādhi of the ocean-treasury of true suchness (*tathatā*) of the hundred thousand secret vajra-bodhi-buddha-natures,
and fulfill all dharmas— the inexhaustible vajra-wisdom and bodhi of the noble nature of all Tathāgatas and all great dharmas.
Therefore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Uttaramati was first able to explain the false conceptualization of consciousness and the noble nature of the Tathāgata; he who,
through the union of these two meanings, matured the great Dharma of Bodhi, the Vajra-like Noble Wisdom.
This is called the Bodhisattva’s cultivation and study of the Tathāgata’s noble nature, through which their understanding and practice become unified;
thus they are able to realize the ten great dharmas of enlightenment within the dharma-realm of their own being.
Thereafter, one cultivates the entry into and realization of the contemplation of the non-substantiality of unshakable nirvāṇa.
How does one employ skillful means to realize and enter this contemplation of non-substantiality?
A bodhisattva must first, with the mind, contemplate and illuminate the quiescent nature of reality.
Upon awakening, he enters the meditative attainment of cessation;
he realizes and perceives the purity of the nature of mind and consciousness,
and through being solely pure and solely serene, he realizes and perceives the noble nature.
The self-nature is suchness, a single path of tranquil purity.
Awakening to and reaching the original source, one reflects back and perceives stillness.
It is only illumination, only brilliance; only brilliance, only purity; only tranquility, only sageliness.
This is called the Bodhisattva’s attainment of entry into the contemplation of immovable nirvāṇa and the absence of intrinsic nature.
If there is any bodhisattva who relies upon this superior intention of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, [they shall likewise attain it].
Those who practice and study this dharma-gate will swiftly realize the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of a Buddha;
therefore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Uttaramati—
For the sake of all sentient beings within the dharma-realm throughout the three periods of time,
he clearly expounds and proclaims the secret Vajra-Bodhisattva accomplishment of the immovable nirvana of non-nature.
May all bodhisattvas and all sentient beings of future,
distant ages swiftly enter the Tathāgata’s holy nature through the samādhi of the contemplation of non-substantiality.
Because he had attained the Buddha's Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi,
at that time the Tathāgata then, in due order,
caused the Bodhisattva Dharaṇīdhara to [receive it].
He himself spoke on the gate of practicing contemplative cultivation.
Second, from the lower direction, there was the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Lokeśvara, a Bodhisattva of the celestial world of the Vajradhātu ground.
Facing the Tathāgata himself,
one then expounds the contemplation of the secret dharma before all the bodhisattvas of the present.
Furthermore, may all bodhisattvas and all sentient beings of the future cultivate and enter the samādhi of the ocean of sarvajñā;
and may they study the contemplation on the true nature of the perfection of patience regarding all the Buddhas’ vajra-bodhi and all secret, profound dharmas.
If a bodhisattva practices according to this gate of contemplation,
they will realize the Tathāgata’s vajra-like samādhi of the boundless ocean of nature.
Relying on this samādhi, they attain entry into the secret bodhi-vajra-holding ground, the samādhi of the ocean of the nature of the world.
From this, through the power of the vow of the Vajra-nature of the Ocean of Sustaining the World, he was established upon the ground of the Vajra-realm;
there arose a world characterized by the marks of the Dharma-treasury, firm in its Vajra-ocean nature, which serves as the foundation.
Being without obstruction and equal to space, they possess no marks of differentiation;
they are all the source, the Vairocana Tathāgata,
within the ocean of the secret dharmatā, which is the adamantine nature of reality, firm and solid.
It establishes the great earth world with its myriad forms;
it is the total basis for all physical forms, marks and signs, sovereign powers,
spiritual responses, transformations, and manifestations.
Through the empowerment of the holy power of the great vows made by Tathāgata Vairocana in previous lives,
all bodhisattvas as well as all sentient beings cultivate the noble path of awakening and liberation.
They have accomplished the maturation of all sentient beings in this world;
they possess the sovereign spiritual power that assists the Buddhas in bringing them to maturity through the unification of all into a single nature;
and they have attained correspondence with the noble wisdom of the samādhis of all Tathāgatas.
May all sentient beings be without exception happy;
may they together enter bodhi and attain full perfection—
all this is due to the deeds of the Tathāgata Vairocana in times past.
Throughout oceans of kalpas, by means of great power of aspiration,
while practicing the bodhisattva path, they have gathered all Buddhas and great bodhisattvas through the four methods of attraction and the performance of the eight great offerings,
thereby embracing the roots of goodness planted during each of their stages on the causal ground.
Having already encompassed them all through various skillful means to teach and bring them to maturity,
they cause all bodhisattvas to be established upon the path of all-encompassing wisdom and the path of all noble lineages.
The path of all vajras and the path of all liberations—
this is called the great, virtuous benefit and skillful means for accomplishing the ocean-treasury of bodhi of all Tathāgatas.
The ocean of vows, the Prajñāpāramitā,
the practices performed by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas during their past causal stages,
and the noble path of complete purity and liberation.
Because they are able to skillfully enter the samādhis of all Buddhas,
they cause those bodhisattvas and all sentient beings to always clearly and distinctly perceive the retribution bodies of the Buddhas.
By the power of resolute conviction, they enter the ocean of the Tathāgata’s nature of merit.
They attain the gates of liberation of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
and through the playful exercise of supernormal powers, they harmonize with the power of their original vows.
Arousing the mind of great compassion, he vows to deliver all sentient beings,
so that they may all take refuge in the Buddhas and achieve the perfect fulfillment of the ocean-like nature of Vajra Bodhi. Therefore,
as was demonstrated to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Lokadhara:
He causes all bodhisattvas to enter and cultivate the practice of the vajra-samādhi, to abide in the patience of the profound Dharma,
and to contemplate the true nature of the pāramitās.
"How may one quickly enter this skillful means and realize this contemplation?
At that time, the Bodhisattva Dhāraṇīdhara should immediately contemplate and observe with his own mental eye.
Entering the nature of one's own mind, which is the essence of the Dharma-realm,
one attains the vision of the essence of the self-nature mind and realizes the Tathāgata’s vajra-like holy nature.
Thoroughly penetrating the emptiness of dharmas with boundless awakened wisdom,
one contemplates that great wisdom through the great tranquility of the wisdom of emptiness;
entering the mind, the mind is empty, and realizing emptiness, one further transcends emptiness.
The mind is like empty space and identical to the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*).
To clearly perceive one's nature is called "realizing the self-nature," which is the dharma-body of noble wisdom; this is the fundamental nature of the mind.
Its spiritual function is sovereign, pure, void, unified, and tranquil; its dharmas are identical to the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*), true thusness (*tathatā*), and the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
If one realizes this nature, it is called the fundamental source-nature, true reality, and the non-substantiality of noble wisdom. Therefore,
when the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dhāraṇīdhara was on the causal ground in the past,
he established his original great vow.
Together with Vairocana Tathāgata, may all bodhisattvas and all sentient beings be delivered,
and together enter this vow— the Buddha’s noble nature, the adamantine bodhi, the great vow-practice, the Buddha-samyaksamādhi, and the profound dharma-patience pāramitā.

Through wisdom and conduct, they simultaneously realize the ten kinds of noble practices and the illusion-like samādhi.

free from conscious ideation, its intrinsic nature is pure.
Suchness is truly quiescent, signless, and wishless;

Second, through cultivation and maintenance, one attains entry into the stage of the Dharma (dharmapada) and cultivates progress toward Bodhi.

Transcending the two truths, one realizes the single essence of true suchness (*tathatā*),

Fourth, they enter the Buddha’s noble practice, which is of a single essence with the nature of reality;

Entering into conventional truth (*saṃvṛti-satya*), one practices the bodhisattva path.

Their nature is identical to true suchness and the illusion-like samādhi.

Attaining the realization of bodhi and entering the path of the Buddhas—

Yet, while following sounds, one does not cling to the marks of sound;

This is the illusion-like bliss.

To practice clearly and with full understanding according to what has been taught—

as well as all secret samādhis, [are so named].
In reality, nothing can be apprehended; like an illusion, there is no fixed nature.

for [the body] is a transformation produced by the flow of karma.

All phenomena and characteristics lack any fixed nature,

Bodhisattvas and bhikṣus should all act in this manner, for all activities are collectively like an illusion.

Chapter Four: The Manifestation of the Teaching for Cultivation and Practice on Entering the Dharma and Seeing the Path by All Worthies and Sages. This is the fourth chapter, "The Manifestation of the Teaching for Cultivation and Practice on Entering the Dharma and Seeing the Path by All Worthies and Sages. At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni...
In the great assembly at the Great Dharma Site of Jetavana Monastery in Śrāvastī,
there were ten billion bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and fifty trillion śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
There were eighty trillion bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, śrāmaṇeras, and śikṣamāṇās—the fourfold assembly of disciples;
fifty trillion nāgas, spirits, and the eight classes of beings;
and eight thousand billion ghosts, gods, and yakṣas.

There were seventy trillion world-protectors, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, and various universal monarchs (cakravartin); eight thousand billion celestial lords and the hosts of the gods of the six heavens of the desire realm;
and ninety thousand billion Great Brahmā Heavenly Kings and their celestial hosts.
There were forty trillion world-ruling monarchs, great kings, and minor kings,
as well as thirty trillion sons and daughters of good family.
At that time, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni—
In the great assembly, he occupied the lion throne,
sat upon a pedestal of a hundred jewels,
and entered the vajra-samādhi.
He emitted the light of the Golden Samādhi,

which universally illumined all the Buddha-lands throughout the great trichiliocosm and the dharma-realm, reaching as many Buddha-fields in other directions as there are atoms in a buddha-field, such that no place was left unpenetrated.

having seen this light, their bodies and minds were awakened.

There are hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of such great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
At that time, within the assembly of bodhisattvas,
there was a bodhisattva named Universal Eye (Samantacakṣus).
He prostrated himself at the feet of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Where is Samantabhadra Bodhisattva now?
The World-Honored One replied, “Universal Eye,
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is currently present here within this assembly at the site of enlightenment.”
He drew near to me and stood at my left side, remaining there without ever shifting.
At that time, Universal Eye and the other bodhisattvas again surveyed the assembly gathered at the site of enlightenment.

The Bodhisattva Universal Eye addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, we who are here now..."

The Buddha said, "So it is, Universal Eye.
Sons of good family, for what reason are you unable to see him?"
The World-Honored One said to Samantacakṣus:
"The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra dwells in the body of the dharma-nature;
it is profoundly deep, subtle, and ineffable to behold."
Therefore, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra has attained a vajra-nature body of boundless wisdom.
The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra abides in the Lion’s Vigorous Stride Samādhi.
Abiding in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi,
they attain unexcelled bodhi and sovereign supernormal powers,
becoming identical to the pure Dharma-body of the Tathāgata.
Having realized the unimpeded limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*),
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva abides in the ten kinds of noble nature and noble power of the Tathāgatas;
he takes as his body the *dharmadhātu*, which is the treasury of wisdom.
All Buddhas, Tathāgatas, together protect and keep him in mind.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, before the presence of the Tathāgata,
manifested the sovereign spiritual power of holy nature.
In a single moment of thought, they are able to realize and enter all Buddha-lands as numerous as motes of dust within the trichiliocosm;
the Buddhas of the three periods of time are unimpeded and undifferentiated,
for their wisdom-body and dharma-body are of the same substance and identical nature.
Therefore, the Buddha’s speech is the Universal Eye;
yet you, all you in the assembly, are unable to see it.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Universal Eye heard the Tathāgata speak of the profoundly deep, holy wisdom and the subtle, pure body of merit of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
The Bodhisattva Universal Eye then, in the presence of the Tathāgata,
entered ten thousand asaṃkhyeya samādhis. By the power of these samādhis,
he further shone forth universally and observed with insatiable longing.
Desiring to see Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
Puyan observed him once more, yet he was still unable to behold him,
as were all the other great assemblies of bodhisattvas.
Neither of them was able to see the physical form, marks, or signs of Samantabhadra.
Therefore, the Bodhisattva Universal Eye arose from samādhi and approached the presence of the Tathāgata.
He addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One, I have already entered ten thousand *asaṃkhyeya* samādhis,
seeking and wishing to see the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra;
yet, in the end, I am unable to perceive his physical marks, his signs of excellence, or the conduct of Samantabhadra."
Furthermore, regarding this bodily action, vocal action, and mental action—
whether sitting, standing, walking, or staying— they sought them everywhere but saw nothing at all.
The Buddha said, "So it is, so it is."
The Buddha said to the Bodhisattva Universal Eye:
"For example, among the various illusory manifestations within an illusion,
even the dwelling place where they appear cannot be perceived."
How much more so for Samantabhadra Bodhisattva!
His secret physical form is identical to space;
his body is secret, his speech is secret, and his mind is also secret.
One should know that the sovereign power of the holy Samantabhadra is inconceivable;
within the dharma-realm, he is able to enter and emerge,
see and manifest, conceal and vanish.
Why is this? The realm of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is profoundly deep;
it cannot be compared, measured, conceived, or fathomed.
Only a Buddha can know it, for it is immeasurable.
To speak briefly of the essential point:
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, by means of the samādhi of adamantine wisdom, universally enters the holy nature, which is identical to the dharma-nature and the dharma-realm of all phenomena;
he has no dependence whatsoever upon any world.
Samantabhadra knows that the bodies and minds of all sentient beings are entirely empty;
they neither go nor come, their nature being identical to that of Samantabhadra—
without distinction, without dependence, and without fabrication.
Its nature is without movement or change, reaching the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu).
It arrives at the ultimate limit, like empty space;
the nature of empty space cannot be perceived.
The body and mind of Samantabhadra are likewise so.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra amidst the great assembly:

Therefore, the Tathāgata asked Samantabhadra:

during the void kalpa of immeasurable Buddha-fields and worlds."

"Since beginningless time, who has been our teacher and guide,

O Mañjuśrī, Great Being Bodhisattva!
Then, amidst the great assembly, he raised his voice in a loud sound and declared:
