Translated by Amoghavajra by Imperial Decree: At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata,
together with the great assembly of all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
sequentially expounded the gate of the contemplation on the equality of the Tathāgata’s vajra-noble nature.
Third, how does one sequentially enter the gate of equality?
First, by entering the contemplation of the syllable *pa*, one realizes the meaning of the fundamental reality being unstained, unattached, and free from defilement.
This is the Dharma-realm gate of the equality of *tathatā* (suchness) taught by Ratnasambhava Tathāgata.
Within this section, two chapters are expounded.

The first is the fifth chapter, "The Decisive Determination of the Ground of Mind through the Teaching on the Secret Method of Returning to and Stopping within Contemplative Insight and Illumination of the Dharma-nature.
The above constitutes one chapter of the teaching.
Regarding this teaching, the "Chapter on Contemplating and Resolving the Mind-Ground" is to be combined with the secret instructions on the mind-ground within the maṇḍala;
it should not be explained openly in this sūtra.
First, it is explained separately within the "Chapter on the Holy Nature of Yoga" (*Yogācāryabhūmi-viniścaya-saṃgrahaṇī*) as the secret instruction on the gate of contemplation.
Second, later on, there is the sixth chapter, which expounds how all bodhisattvas train in the Tathāgata’s samādhi, wherein the holy nature permeates and bestows its grace.
The Tathāgata shall now, in due order, speak the Chapter on Secret Penetration and Empowerment.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni was in the great assembly at the site of enlightenment.

The entire great assembly, including the various devas, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the fourfold assembly, the Mahābrahmā devas, the nāgas and spirits of the eight classes, and sons and daughters of good family.
He beheld the Tathāgata entering the samādhi of the pure dharma-realm of the suchness-limit (bhūtakoṭi),
emitting the golden light of the noble nature-samādhi (*ārya-dhātu-samādhi*),
which illuminated the dharma-realm-nature-body, the physical marks and signs, and the limbs and members of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Within each and every pore, there are inconceivable,
unspeakably unspeakable oceans of Buddha-fields; within each ocean of fields,
there appear as many Buddhas as there are atoms in a mote of dust, arising in the world.
He was surrounded by a great assembly of bodhisattvas, while the Buddhas,
the World-Honored Ones, were instructing sentient beings as well as all the great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, one sees the Tathāgata enter the non-reliant Vairocana,
whose pure Dharma-body is equal to space,
manifesting infinite bodies through his body of wisdom.
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva emerges from the Tathāgata’s body of immeasurable wisdom;
he travels everywhere to the pure lands of the ten directions to serve all Buddhas and enters the dharma-realm of all Buddhas.
He manifests an immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable mastery,
a body of wisdom whose nature is the dharmas of supernormal powers.
Abiding in the gateways of immeasurable omniscience, he thoroughly understands all phenomena through the radiance of his wisdom.
They attain fearlessness regarding all phenomena.
Whatever they expound shall endure until the end of the future, their eloquence being inexhaustible;
through great wisdom, they open the gates of dhāraṇī.
The eye of wisdom is pure and penetrating; the Dharma-eye is boundless.
Entering the profound realm of phenomena, one attains the sphere of wisdom, which is without obstruction and without limit.
Ultimate tranquility is like empty space.
Such are the worlds of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
as well as the Tuṣita Heaven palaces and the great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas therein.
He also beheld the manifestations of the sovereign spiritual transformations of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
he also beheld all the Tathāgatas’ miraculous powers and spiritual penetrations within all the pure lands of those Buddhas, as well as all the bodhisattvas.
All such Buddhas and Bodhisattvas likewise planted roots of goodness together with Tathāgata Vairocana in the distant past.
Having cultivated the path of the bodhisattvas and practiced the vows and conduct of Samantabhadra,
they have fully awakened to and entered the profound liberation of the sovereign power of all buddhas,
attaining a body of the non-differentiated nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*).
They equally enter the ocean-treasury of the noble nature of all Buddhas' pure lands and abide therein;
all of this is through the sovereign power of the Tathāgata's sanctity,
for the spiritual power of the Dharma-realm of the noble nature is boundless.
The merit is immeasurable and inconceivable.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, within the great assembly,
addressed the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the fourfold assembly, the bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, the sons and daughters of good family, and all sentient beings.
Therefore, if there is a bodhisattva who cultivates the secrecy of the body and diligently practices contemplation,
they will follow the vast and great vows and practices formerly undertaken by Samantabhadra.
For one who enters into the essential nature of the three secrets of sentient beings and practices the thirty-branch samādhi-contemplation of the gateway of the Vajra Three Secrets,
within each and every branch of the contemplation:
Entering into the fundamental nature of sentient beings—
the dharmadhātu, the mind-nature, and the true suchness of wisdom and insight—
one swiftly bestows empowerment and causes them to abide therein.
He realized the Vajra Samādhi.
At that time, through the power of wisdom and the vajra-nature of the original vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
all sentient beings were enabled to realize the gate of liberation of bodhi.
At that time, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni addressed Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, saying:
"You have always dwelt within the ocean of skillful means of the inconceivable, profound, and secret samādhi of the dharmakāya of all Buddhas—the holy nature of the vajra-dharmadhātu."
It is identical with the Tathatā-dharmadhātu, the ocean-treasury of the bodhi-merit of the noble nature of all Tathāgatas;
that is to say, through the empowerment of the practice of sentient beings,
they swiftly attain the samādhi of the secret samaya, which is the seal of the realization-body (dharmakāya) and liberation through the three mysteries.
There are several gates [to this].
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva said:
"I have hitherto received the sacred instructions and teachings of the Buddha."
"Practice the thirty secret contemplation gates.
Thus did the World-Honored One speak to Samantabhadra.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata spoke of himself:
Regarding the thirty secret contemplation gates,
we shall first address the ten branches of the first gate, the Secret Body.
The Tathāgata has analyzed each one individually so that one may practice this contemplation.
Then Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
together with the ten great bodhisattvas,
again prostrated themselves before the Tathāgata and said:

"What are the ten kinds of adamantine sacred nature secret seals (*vajra-ārya-dharmatā-guhya-mudrā*) for the body-secret, the ten branches of the bodhi-contemplation for practicing and realizing the sacred nature, and the samādhi gateways?
The Buddha addressed Mahāsamantabhadra, saying:"
One shall be accompanied by ten great bodhisattvas as leaders;
sharing the same vows, they shall cultivate and realize the holy nature, and through the empowerment of the holy power, enter the mind-nature and bodies of all sentient beings.
Together with all bodhisattvas, you shall be their leader,
guiding and receiving sentient beings so that they awaken and enter into bodhi.
What are called the ten kinds of samādhi-contemplations on the liberation doors of the secret seals of the body that accord with bodhi?
The first was named the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra-vikrama;
he entered the great tranquil and pure wisdom of Vairocana and emerged from that pure wisdom.
Returning to the wisdom of the three mysteries of the self-nature of sentient beings,
the mind-ground of sentient beings is identical to that of the Tathāgata;
it is the holy nature of the entire dharma-realm and the bodhi of all Buddhas.
The Seal of the Body Empowered by the Holy Nature that Subdues the Minds of Sentient Beings:
a gateway to liberation through the wisdom-body that swiftly realizes ultimate transcendence from the ocean of suffering of birth and death.
The second was the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Crest-King of the Supreme Site of Enlightenment.
He had entered the samādhi of the ocean of the nature of all Buddhas-Tathāgatas and their pure lands, perceiving every single realm within the holy power of the Buddha.
He went everywhere to all Tathāgatas to receive instruction on the supreme realm of merit of the Mahāyāna secret samādhi,
and entered the body-secret samādhi-mudrā through the empowerment of the dharmadhātu.
Because he has accomplished the Dharma-body and is free from change, he has attained the gate of liberation.
Third is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Mahāvīrya-vajranābhi,
who enters the samādhi of knowing the ultimate quiescence of all Tathāgatas.
He causes [beings] to enter the secret bodhi of the nature-body of sentient beings;
he attains the seal of the empowerment body for all bodhisattva stages in their established positions;
and he enters the vajra-samādhi of the gateway to the three secrets.
Because they universally fulfill all great vows of myriad practices,
they realize the liberation door of the ocean-like nature of phenomena.
Fourth is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Blue Lotus Eye.
Entering the samādhi of attaining perfect enlightenment as the heart-mind of all Buddhas,
within that samādhi, he universally manifests the seals of the bodies empowered by the immeasurable sublime dharmas of Tathāgatas throughout dharma-realms as numerous as atoms.
The liberation door of manifesting the dharma-body to enter the nature of sentient beings and establish the seeds of bodhi without obstruction;
fifth is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Bodhivyuha (Bodhi Banner).

They realize and enter a state where the moon-like, luminous, pure, and clear marks of light universally manifest throughout all dharma-realms; through unimpeded sounds, they expound the teachings to awaken sentient beings to their own cognitive nature, thereby attaining entry into samādhi.
He expounds and explains the subtle and secret meaning.
Through the empowerment of the body-seal (*kāyamudrā*), he causes [beings] to realize the holy nature of the dharmadhātu and to witness all buddha-fields.
They fully manifest the inconceivable, non-differentiated wisdom of total purity,
the gate of liberation that is sovereign and unobstructed.
Sixth is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Vimalagarbha.
He entered the samādhi of the nature of true suchness-wisdom, which is immovable and unchanging within the realm of the Tathāgata Radiance of the Wisdom of All Buddhas;
he entered into all the Buddha-lands as numerous as atoms.
They see all the boundless great bodhisattvas,
who are all able to empower them to enter the body-seal (kāyamudrā) and penetrate the essential nature of sentient beings.
They swiftly and rapidly realize and achieve the enlightenment of awakening,
the liberation door of the sovereign realm of supernormal powers.
Seventh is the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Sarvatathāgatavikurvaṇamaṇirājaketudhvajajālacchatramañjuśrīcūḍa.
Entering the samādhi of the light of wisdom that realizes the single characteristic and non-differentiation of the dharma-realm;
with a single thought, through the empowerment of noble wisdom,
one manifests the seals of the body and perceives the kalpas of formation and destruction throughout the three periods of past, future, and present.
The gate of liberation that is the equality of all phenomena, as numerous as atoms, within the purity of True Suchness.
Eighth is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Śāntiprabha.
He enters the samādhi of the Tathāgata’s vajra-wisdom that assists sentient beings in various ways to advance toward the noble path of bodhi;
he enters the seal of the empowered body,
causing them to enter the ocean of the nature of the self-nature of all bodhisattvas’ faculties.
Each entered the inconceivable gate of liberation of the spiritual power of the samādhi realm of their own wisdom.
Ninth was the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Āryajñānāśugajinendrarāja.
They enter the signless samādhi of the great supernormal power of the Dharma-body within the inexhaustible Dharma-realm and space-realm.
By means of the seal of the empowerment-body,
they cause various wisdom-bodies to be manifested through the power of the sages, appearing in response to immeasurable sacred wisdom and entering the nature of all sentient beings.
Throughout all buddha-fields,
he manifests the gate of noble wisdom and liberation— the ocean of the nature of the boundless dharma-realm of all buddhas,
tathāgatas. The tenth is named the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Dharmasāgaragarjitasvararāja.
Entering samādhi, they attain the power of all bodhisattva stages to achieve perfect enlightenment, entering the liberation-samādhi of the Buddhas;
they manifest the power of practice, vows, and conduct of the Samantabhadra-dharmaparyāya for all bodhisattvas.
One sequentially practices the contemplation of the secret samādhi of the original vow,
empowers the body with mudrās,
and enters the bodhi-samādhi of the nature-wisdom of all bodhisattvas.
Through the vast and noble conduct, skillful means, and power of aspiration,
he causes all sentient beings to swiftly realize the gate of liberation of unsurpassed bodhi.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva...
Having made extensive great vows before the Tathāgata, he entered into samādhi;
together with ten great bodhisattva mahāsattvas as his leaders,
he vowed to practice and uphold these great vows to establish himself in bodhi.
Abiding within the Buddha-nature of the physical dimensions of all sentient beings,
it is of one essence with the ocean of the nature of True Suchness (*tathatā*),
sustaining and empowering all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Entering the Body Seal advances one toward Bodhi;
therefore, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
at that time, stood before the Tathāgata.
He then entered the ocean of samādhis of the vajra-dharmadhātu-nature;
within the ocean of the measure of his own dharmatā-body,
he manifested buddha-nature worlds as numerous as motes of dust.
He instructs all the great bodhisattvas and all sentient beings,
as numerous as motes of dust;
furthermore, he manifests the Tathāgata sitting upon a lion throne beneath the Bodhi tree.
Equal in measure to empty space and pervading the entire Dharma-realm,
the great precious lotus of the Vajra-dharma ocean shall manifest its signs within the ocean of the suchness-nature.
All are contained within the body of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
within the wisdom and sagely virtue of the Dharma-nature, there is no obstruction.
His sublime and holy power brings mastery over supernatural faculties.
At that time, the Tathāgata praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra:
"Excellent, excellent! You are able to manifest the inconceivable power and profound subtlety of the realm of all Buddhas."
He entered the samādhi of the ocean-like nature of the merits of all Buddhas, which gives rise to inexhaustible,
vast vows and practices. Because it is the great vow of the Tathāgata,
it is inconceivable and beyond all measure.
Because the ocean of the profound, adamantine, and holy nature is unspeakably unspeakable,
at that time the Tathāgata addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Pure Virtue Sublime Light.
You should travel everywhere to the bodhimandas of the holy virtues of all Buddhas— the nature-sea of the dharma-realm—
and there inquire after and receive the secret dharma-gates of all Tathāgatas, namely the teachings on the samādhi of oral mantra.
Śuddhaguṇasuprabha, together with the ten great beings— the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who serve as his leaders—
aroused vast vows and practiced the conduct of Samantabhadra.
He thereby attained entry into the nature of the body and mind of all sentient beings' spiritual lineages.
The empowerment of the Sage’s power brings the secret of speech to realization within the ground of the mind.
For those who enter the contemplation of the ten-limbed samādhi, there is the unimpeded eloquence of wisdom and the great intellectual skill of the secret mantras and mudrās of speech.
There are several gateways.
The Great Being Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Pure Virtue Wondrous Light (Vimalaguṇaprabha) is,
in fact, ten such Great Beings Bodhisattvas.
I prostrate to the Tathāgata and speak these words:
there are all the Buddhas of the ten directions who,
with one voice, together proclaim the oral secret mantras, mudrās, and samādhi-visualizations.
There are ten gates of liberation for the practice of empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*).
What are these ten dharma-gates?
They are the attainment of entry into the essential nature (*dharmatā*) of sentient beings.
They shall swiftly attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. What are the ten?
The first is named the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Universal Manifestation of All Names and Sounds of the Three Times Topknot.
Entering samādhi through the empowerment of the holy power of the oral mudrā,
he entered into the pure nature of all sentient beings and realized the Samādhi of the Illumination of the Most Victorious Lamp-Flame of Universal Virtue.
They attain the samādhi of the Vajra-Wisdom Illumination that Universally Surpasses the Ocean of Buddha-Nature, manifesting the inexhaustible Dharma-realm within a single thought-moment;
they swiftly attain the liberation gate of perfect enlightenment.
The second was named Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvabodhigarjitaghoṣasvara.
He entered a samādhi empowered by noble wisdom, and through the seal of the secret speech, he entered into every atom.
He attained the teaching for realizing the supreme samādhis of the various dhāraṇīs;
he transformed sentient beings as numerous as the atoms of incalculable eons, maturing them through the contemplation of inconceivable samādhi.
The third is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrajñānaprabhāveśvararāja, who enters samādhi and,
through the empowerment of noble wisdom, [manifests] the oral secret mudrā.
He entered the Samādhi of the Universal Radiance Lion-King’s Vigorous Display of the Vajra Banner,
realized the empowerment of the vajra-nature of the sages,
and caused him to cultivate the supreme merit of a bodhisattva to adorn the pure lands of all Buddhas.
The liberation door of manifesting Buddha-lands as numerous as all atoms,
and manifesting Tathāgatas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to bring sentient beings to maturity;
fourth, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Sarvapraṇidhānasāgaraghoṣaratnarājamaulī.
Entering the samādhi empowered by the noble nature of the oral mudrā,
he realized the samādhi of the universally wondrous jewel-flame and sublime light,
attaining the unimpeded realm of the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas.
The liberation door of pure dharmatā, right view, right knowledge, and non-delusion.
Fifth is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Wisdom Banner (Jñānaketu),
who enters samādhi through the empowerment of noble virtue and the seal of the secret speech, and realizes the Samādhi of the Universal Victorious Merit-Ocean Banner.
They enter into the dharma-realm assembly of bodhisattvas within the lotus-ocean treasury of all atom-sized buddha-fields,
manifesting inconceivable spiritual powers and the purity of the noble nature.
They enter the minds of all sentient beings,
causing them to realize and enter the pure land of the Tathāgata’s Dharma-nature,
and attain the gate of liberation that is the ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas.
Sixth is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Buddhagotravidyāparamottaracaryā.
He entered the samādhi of the empowerment of the holy path through the oral mudrā,
and realized the samādhi of the holy wisdom-body of the Tathāgata Buddha-nature, the illumination of the light of the samādhi of universal wisdom-light.
They enter the ground of the noble nature of all great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
they realize sovereign spiritual powers and follow the Tathāgata in contemplating the profound meaning of the Dharma.
They enter the liberation door of the true nature of *tathatā*, the treasury of the vast dharma-realm.
Seventh is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Universal Sound of All Dharma Realms;
he enters the samādhi of the empowerment of the noble conduct of the secret seal of speech.
He entered the samādhi of the pure, inexhaustible light of merit and majestic power that universally beholds all;
he attained the empowerment arising from the sovereign power to universally enter all mundane and supramundane realms.
All the great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have accomplished the boundless gates of practice of Samantabhadra’s Great Vows, the liberation-gate of the Dharma-realm and empty space.
The eighth is named the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Brahma-Sound Ocean-Vastness.
Entering the samādhi through the empowerment of the noble supernormal powers and the oral mudrā,
one realizes the most supreme samādhi of the universal gate (*samantamukha*),
wherein the two aspects of the conditioned and the unconditioned are equal in their single nature.

Within the dharma-realm, he empowers all bodhisattvas to realize the gate of liberation that is the self-nature nirvana of the supernormal power of the bases of mastery belonging to all buddhas and tathāgatas.
Ninth is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Inexhaustible Pure Eloquence in Preaching the Dharma and Unobstructed Wisdom.
He entered a samādhi empowered by the spiritual power of the noble realm, [employing] the oral seal-mudrā.
He entered the samādhi of the unimpeded wisdom-function of the universal gate character-wheel (*samantamukha-akṣara-cakra*) and empowered all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
enabling them to enter the ineffable secret treasury of the Tathāgata, which comprises all dharma-gates.
They enter the unimpeded wisdom of the consciousness-nature of all sentient beings,
and all attain the liberation door of inexhaustible eloquence through awakening and understanding.
Tenth is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Cakravartirutaśikhin.
Entering samādhi, through the empowerment of the sacred speech and sounds, he attests to the oral secret seal (*mukha-mudrā*) and enters the *Vajraśekhara-samādhi*,
bestowing his grace upon all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
They attain entry into the Noble Eightfold Path that accords with enlightenment;
these bodhisattvas are said to practice the Noble Path of Right View because they remain far removed from all false views.
They give rise to right reflection and abandon deluded discrimination,
for their minds always accord with all correct wisdom.
They constantly practice right speech, remaining free from the four faults of speech and acceding to the words of the sages.
Constantly cultivating right action in order to teach and transform sentient beings so that they may be tamed;
abiding securely in right livelihood, ascetic practices (*dhūta*), and contentment;
and maintaining majestic deportment and noble conduct with thorough correctness and compliance.
The four noble lineages of wisdom for practicing the path to bodhi lead one to enter the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, becoming one with the Tathāgata’s Buddha-mind; thus,
all ten worldly evils and every transgression are forever abandoned.
Arousing the mind of a sentient being, they cause them to apply themselves with right diligence;
they assiduously cultivate all the ascetic practices of a bodhisattva and enter the ten powers of a Buddha without obstruction.
Therefore, with a mind constantly in right mindfulness, one is able to remember and maintain all correct speech, noble wisdom, and vocal sounds;
for this eliminates worldly wrong conduct, worldly wrong livelihood, and the distraction of the mind.
With his mind always in right concentration, he attained the three kinds of mind-made bodies and skillfully entered the inconceivable gates of liberation of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
At that time, there was the Mahāsattva Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Pure Virtue Subtle Light.
Having prostrated and paid homage before the Tathāgata, he entered into samādhi;
he immediately and universally entered the ocean of the dharma-realm of the equality of all Buddhas,
becoming one with the holy nature of the Tathāgatas, which is like space.
It is universally able to encompass tens of millions of dharma-realms as numerous as motes of dust;
all Buddhas of the three periods of time and all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas enter this samādhi together.
Because he enters into the essential nature of sentient beings and, through the power of his sustaining wisdom, causes them all to attain liberation;
at that time, the Tathāgatas of the ten directions together praised the Great Being Bodhisattva Pure Virtue Wondrous Light.
Excellent, excellent! You are well able to bestow the power and nature of the noble ones.
By entering the pure cognitive nature within the bodies and minds of all sentient beings, you advance toward enlightenment and swiftly attain the fruit of Buddhahood.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sāgaraprabhāmahāprabhāsa-mati:
"You should act as the leader for the ten great beings, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas."
Likewise, they cause all sentient beings to enter the ocean of the *dharmadhātu*,
which is the essential nature of Vairocana Tathāgata;
within this ocean of the nature of the *dharmadhātu*, the Tathāgata...
There appeared the world-system known as the Treasury of the Lotus Flower Throne of a Hundred Jewels.
Upon its central throne, there were a thousand petals extending in all directions;
each petal was a world, thus constituting a thousand worlds.
I manifest as a thousand Śākyamunis, each presiding over a thousand worlds.
Furthermore, within a single-leaf world,
there are ten billion Mount Sumerus and ten billion suns and moons.
In ten billion worlds of four continents, across ten billion Jambudvīpas in the south, there were ten billion Bodhisattvas Śākyas,
seated upon thrones of Buddhas atop precious lotuses within the Lotus Treasury World.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata,
together with the ten great beings, the Bodhisattvas Samudrasūryaprabhāmahāprajñā and the others,
collectively entered the Vairocana Lotus-Ocean-Treasury Dharmadhātu-Svabhāva Samādhi.
Furthermore, he causes sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within hundreds of thousands of millions of worlds— as many as the sands of the Ganges and beyond measure—
to realize and witness the ocean of Buddha-nature, the samādhi of the dharma-nature of True Suchness.
The Tathāgata causes his holy power to bestow blessings and increase the fundamental essence,
noble nature, and noble wisdom of all sentient beings.
By means of entering samādhi and being empowered by the noble wisdom of prajñā,
one will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, the entire great assembly...
Together with the ten great beings, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas Sāgaracandraprabha-mahāprajñā and others,
they all bowed their heads to the World-Honored One,
the Tathāgata. The Bodhisattvas, Sāgaracandraprabha and the rest, said:
"Regarding the samādhi of the essential nature of the Buddha’s samādhi:
can all sentient beings enter this samādhi and contemplate it?
The Buddha said to Sāgaracandraprabhāmahāprajñā:
Good son, if there are any sentient beings who can renounce their bodies and lives and have deep faith in the Mahāyāna,
they should then deeply believe in and accept this teaching.
Thus, one attains entry into this teaching of the gate of contemplation for the three secrets of the Vajra.
At that very moment, the ten great beings, such as the Bodhisattva Ocean-Light-Moon Great Radiance Wisdom,
through the secret empowerment of their holy power, awaken the secret of the mind.
It causes the noble nature and noble power to enter into the pure nature of the mental consciousness of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
so that they may swiftly transcend the stage of Buddhahood and rapidly realize bodhi.
What is meant by "entering the ten-limbed Buddha-samādhi-contemplation liberation door of the secret seal of the yoga-intent"?
The first is named the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Manifesting the Realm of All Great Vows and Universal Wisdom Illumination Tathāgata.
Regarding the one who enters the samādhi through the contemplation of the mental secret seal (*manomudrā*):
May this bodhisattva mahāsattva extensively cultivate merit and be sustained by the power of the sages,
entering the Samādhi of the Pure Nature of the Bright Moon of Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom,
thereby realizing the arising of great clear wisdom.
Entering the Buddha-ground of all great Bodhisattvas, they eliminate afflictions;
the three poisons and great maladies are entirely extinguished,

Entering samādhi, he contemplates the empowerment of the noble nature through the secret seal of mental intent,

One enters the dharma-gate of the three mysteries,
causing the mind to swiftly attain the samādhi equal in measure [to all things],

They gather all sentient beings and transport them to the attainment of Buddhahood;

Seventh is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Universal Awakening and Pleasing Voice.
Entering samādhi, he contemplates the empowerment of the noble qualities and the noble nature, entering the samādhi of the mental mudrā;

They attain the samādhi of the treasury of merit and virtue;
they obtain unimpeded wisdom that enters the realm of all Buddhas;
and they cause all bodhisattvas to universally realize the ocean of merits of all Buddhas.
He is able to enter the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena and advance in noble nature, noble wisdom, and noble insight.
He contemplates the gate of liberation that is the buddha-nature (*buddhadhātu*) of all buddhas.
The eighth is named the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Illumination of the Wisdom of Equal Enlightenment Throughout the Three Times.
Entering samādhi, one contemplates the empowerment of noble wisdom and enters the mental mudrā of secret seal;

They enter into a single essence.

Ninth is the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vast Power, Wondrous Enlightenment, and Great Capacity.
Entering samādhi, he contemplates the empowerment of the noble conduct through the mental mudrā,

Swiftly entering into the state of single nature,
his body and noble mind universally realize the Dharma-realm through the samādhi of the vajra-wisdom flame, which is empty and non-apprehensible;

Equal to space, without support or location,
it swiftly reaches the ocean-treasury of the fundamental source and original nature of all sentient beings,

Tenth is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Dharmadhātu-prabhāsa-samantabodhi-āryajñāna.
He entered samādhi and contemplated the empowerment of the power of noble wisdom through the secret seal-mudrā of the mind.
May all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas realize and enter the true mark of *tathatā*,

In a single thought-moment, they are able to recollect events from immeasurable eons;
within that single thought-moment, they fully know the capacities, faculties, and wisdom of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time, as numerous as atoms.
May they swiftly enter all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi;
may they expound the boundless, profound, and wondrous ocean-treasury of all Buddhas;
and may they constantly turn the pure wheel of Dharma, which is secret regarding all phenomena and never regresses.
May all bodhisattvas and all sentient beings alike realize and enter the samādhi of the light of wisdom of the noble nature within the realm of all Buddhas,
and enter the profound Dharma-treasury of sublime, noble insight.

with inexhaustible, supreme, and sovereign supernormal powers,

at that time the Tathāgata Śākyamuni addressed the Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, saying: "Good son, if there is a practitioner..."

One shall attain the realization of Mañjuśrī’s great wisdom and the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra.

they shall not be permitted to enter this *bodhimaṇḍa* again, but must wait for a later, separate occasion before they may enter.
The World-Honored One earnestly and appropriately instructed and informed the various practicing Bodhisattvas and practitioners.
Do not allow this time to pass in vain, merely exhausting yourself with toil.

Upon realizing that the nature of the mind is pure and manifest before one,

one is then able to receive the transmission of the Dharma and enter the great maṇḍala site of the Greatly Pure Empowerment (*abhiṣeka*).
He bestows the gateway of the three secrets of Mahāyāna Yoga:
the contemplation on the dharmatā of suchness within the vajra-samādhi.
Then, having bestowed the dharma, [he continues].
Then one must not be separated from the ācārya.
Why? Because this person who studies the Path must, day by day, engage in gradual discernment during three periods.

For this reason, the Tathāgata has said that among the assembly of bodhisattvas and the fourfold disciples—
monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen— [this is the foremost].
In this age of the Final Dharma, the Buddha's teachings are difficult to hear;
it is likewise difficult to encounter them now that they have been seen and heard.
This is the fruit of what was cultivated through many kalpas of prior study and practice.
Once the practitioner has received the initiation, they must never again regress or separate from the ācārya.
They must always remain close to and make offerings to the Tathāgata and all the bodhisattvas; therefore, this should be understood.
The instructions for the site of enlightenment (maṇḍala) consist of four types of meanings:
correspondence of time and place, correspondence of practice, and correspondence of the teaching of the Dharma.
One who intends to construct a site of enlightenment and wishes to establish it must require five concentric courtyards.

one may instead arrange four gates,
each guarded by four celestial kings who act as protectors of the boundary.

At the four corners of the altar, place water jars for arghya offerings,
and also set up incense tables at the four gates along with incense burners.
Furthermore, install precious banners, streamers, and canopies.
At the four gates, burn incense and light lamps of ghee and fragrant oil.
Above, place a canopy for the site of enlightenment and a precious celestial parasol.
One should fashion an eight-petaled lotus flower.
Within that maṇḍala, one must first prepare fresh food and drink every day.
Within the maṇḍala, offerings shall be made without interruption.
Those who enter the practice hall— namely the assembly of monks and others—
as well as the Dharma-preaching master and the ācārya, must not take any of these offered foods.
It may be consumed even by those who have not entered the maṇḍala.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata addressed Mañjuśrī, saying:
"Good son, the secret Dharma of the Tathāgatas is truly difficult to encounter."
In the age of the Final Dharma, it is difficult to encounter and difficult to hear [this teaching].
If there is a preceptor-ācārya who is not present within the ritual site for receiving the Dharma, [the transmission cannot take place].
Regarding those who falsely speak of the Tathāgata’s secrets—
the secret treasury of the Dharma of samādhi and contemplation—
such persons are fond of seeking fame and profit, and they speak falsely through flattery and deceit.
The one who speaks it incurs the four grave offenses;
the one who listens incurs the offense of obstructing the Path in every lifetime and falls into hell.
They shall never hear the Dharma of the True Teaching.
Therefore, the fourfold assembly— monks, nuns, and virtuous men and women—
should not recklessly speak of the Tathāgata’s secret teachings.
If there are any bodhisattvas or members of the fourfold assembly who have received and attained the Tathāgata’s secret and wondrous Dharma,
they must constantly and unfailingly make offerings throughout the four seasons.
While walking, reciting, or sitting in meditation,
one should always practice with diligence and not allow oneself to become indolent.
At that time, the Tathāgata spoke of the various manifestations of the delusive illusions of the heavenly demons.

by eating only once every seven days, they shall attain fearlessness.

or forms of Bodhisattvas, devas, Brahmā, or Śakra; or else the forms of nāgas,
spirits, or malevolent ghosts, as well as the forms of boys and girls.

or one may smell a wondrous fragrance from the air,
or hear the recitation of dharanis.

and some hear the sounds of music dedicated to the recollection of the Buddha.
At that time, these luminous manifestations shall be further explained.
They may cause the practitioner to remain unmoving in a state of delusive concentration,
or to give rise to anger, or to become stained by attachment to pleasant objects, or to engage in conceptualization, grasping, and clinging.

or light may appear in a dark room like the sun;
or white and red lights may appear, as well as various malevolent insects.

some cause people to be intelligent and clear-headed, while others cause them to be dull-witted.
Such transformations are all due to celestial demons or malevolent spirits entering the mind.
They create conditions and circumstances that act as obstacles on the path for practitioners,
causing them to advance and retreat and thus fail to achieve the fruit of the Way;
at death, they cause them to enter the palace of Māra and become his retinue.
For this reason, the Tathāgata has said that these are all manifestations of demonic illusions.
Through shifting transformations and the movement of thoughts, one cannot attain right concentration;
furthermore, they enter into people's minds, causing them to falsely claim clever discernment and fraudulent knowledge of past lives.
This causes one to see all illusory appearances and the events of birth and death throughout the succession of lifetimes.
One should recognize that the various signs of good and evil are illusions created by Māra;
they have no connection to true wisdom, being merely manifestations displayed by the mind alone, so do not grasp at external conditions.
Practitioners must certainly not grasp at signs or become attached to them within the realm of dreams or before their very eyes;
for such movements of the mind provoke fear and dread.
Consequently, one will be obstructed by heavenly demons, ghosts, and spirits.
A practitioner of right view must constantly and attentively contemplate the nature of the mind, perceiving that the nature of the mind is quiescent.
The nature of the mind is devoid of substance; do not grasp at its appearances.
Thus, there will be no objective realms and no causes or conditions for deluded thoughts.
For this reason, the practitioner should practice with diligent vigor.
If you truly do not regress, nor become indolent or lazy,

To awaken to the source of the fundamental mind is what is called clearly seeing the nature of afflictions;
this is called the nature of bodhi.
The nature of bodhi is the Dharmakāya Buddha.
Therefore, the World-Honored One addressed the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas:
"All sentient beings who seek unexcelled bodhi..."
A bodhisattva should always cultivate and maintain all the awakenings of the Tathāgata.
These "all awakenings" are called the "single awakening," which is the realization that all sensory consciousnesses are empty, quiescent, and unarisen.
Why is this? Because the definitive nature is fundamentally without movement.
The Buddha said: "All objective spheres are originally empty;
all consciousnesses are by nature originally emptiness."
All objects and consciousnesses are fundamentally empty;
how can one speak of "seeing"?
The Buddha said: "To see [them] is itself delusion.
Why? Because all phenomena are fundamentally empty by nature;
they are without arising and without marks, having never existed from the beginning."
Fundamentally, they do not name themselves and are entirely empty and quiescent.
The characteristics of all phenomena are likewise so;
the bodies of all sentient beings are likewise so.
Since the body itself does not endure for long, how could there be any vision?
The Buddha said: Because it is fundamentally pure from the beginning, this is called "original enlightenment" (mūla-bodhi).
This enlightened nature of the fundamental purity is transparent and reaches everywhere.
Therefore, it is called the fulfillment of the Dharma-body and the Wisdom-body.
The Buddha said: "All sentient beings should employ *vitarka* (initial inquiry) and *vicāra* (sustained investigation).
They should awaken to the fact that the essence of the original mind-nature is quiescent and unarisen."
Because it is free from the defilements of sentient beings;
because it awakens to the primordial stillness that is free from the nature of nirvana;
and because it awakens to the correspondence with all phenomena, being without abiding or movement regarding any phenomenon.
Because they are unmoving and non-abiding, like bodhi;
just as, for example, a vaidūrya jewel reflects colors accordingly,
yet remains a single entity without discrimination.
The Buddha-nature of the Tathāgata is present according to the dispositions of all beings and is entirely pure;
the virtuous response of sentient beings is likewise so.
If a Bodhisattva realizes that the mind has no abiding place and neither enters nor exits, [this is the realization].
Because they have attained the same pure Buddha-consciousness as Oṃ-ma-ra,
the Buddha spoke to the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the fourfold assembly of disciples— bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās.
Those who practice the sacred nature of bodhi, the secret of the Tathāgata’s three vajra mysteries,
will swiftly and profoundly enter into realization of the Tathāgata’s Buddha-mind,
and thereby quickly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Therefore, the Tathāgata addressed the entire assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas:
"You should practice and study this.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni—
From this Jambudvīpa world,
he then returned to that higher realm to speak of the past,
specifically regarding his time in the fourth dhyāna stage within the palace of the Heavenly King Maheśvara.
Together with a great assembly of immeasurable, unspeakably unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* atoms of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,
as well as immeasurable Great Brahmā Lords and their retinues of Brahmā hosts, within that great assembly.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni was in the palace of the Heavenly King.
Within a pavilion made of a hundred kinds of precious mani-jewels,
the Tathāgata sat upon a jeweled throne of a hundred precious lotuses.
The World-Honored One sat upon his seat in the full lotus posture and entered the Samādhi of the Dharmadhātu of the Essential Nature of All Buddhas, which is like Space.
Arising from this samādhi, he emitted thousands of billions of vajra-true-limit-and-real-nature samādhi lights of space.

The light illuminates all Buddhas throughout worlds as numerous as the atoms of a thousand billion worlds, who have entered the samādhi of the adamantine bodhi, the suchness of the limit of reality, and the noble power and noble nature.
He caused all the Buddhas to appear, providing assistance and bearing witness.
Thereupon, he further illumined the hundred trillion palaces of purple-gold adamant light within the Lotus-Treasury World-Ocean.
One clearly perceives the Tathāgata Vairocana—
the dharmakāya, the jñānakāya, and the holy nature of the dharmadhātu;
the treasury of true thusness (tathatā) is without interior or exterior.
Sharing the same sacred wisdom as all Buddhas and Vajras,
the single nature of bodhi pervades everywhere.
At that time, it was the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
Together with the Tathāgata Vairocana of the common nature,
he dwells within the Palace of Vajra Radiance in the Lotus Dharma-Treasury World of hundreds of thousands of millions of worlds,
remaining together in the Vajra Samādhi.
Abiding in the samādhi of the nature of the noble powers,
at that time the World-Honored One Śākyamuni, by means of the supernatural power of his noble nature,
secretly informed Vairocana Tathāgata.
Thereafter, the Tathāgata requested that, for the sake of all bodhisattvas and all sentient beings,
he would explain the cultivation and realization of the Buddha’s vajra-bodhi samādhi.
At that time, Śākyamuni arose from samādhi and earnestly and repeatedly entreated Vairocana Tathāgata for the sake of all bodhisattvas and all sentient beings.
He then expounded the Dharma-gate of the Mind-Ground, the Path of the Fundamental Self-Nature Wisdom of the Buddha. At that time,
Vairocana became Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
He simultaneously manifested a thousand Śākyamunis,
as well as all the bodhisattvas such as the Bodhisattva Mahājñānābhijña,
along with Mahābrahmā, the various devas, and the fourfold assembly.
Listen attentively, listen attentively;
I shall now explain for you once more how all Buddhas and all Bodhisattvas,
in the past, cultivated and practiced the five noble wisdoms of the Buddhas to enter the ground of the mind.
The practice of the samādhi of the secret essence is inconceivable and ineffable.
Having entered the vajra-bodhi, the fruit of Buddhahood,
at that time the World-Honored One, the Muni, spoke these words.
Vairocana first appeared in the world long ago;
in the presence of that Tathāgata Vairocana,
I and all bodhisattvas and all sentient beings of the past cultivated the practice of contemplation together, entering into the Buddha-nature.
The path to Bodhi through noble wisdom reaches its source;
its self-nature is pure illumination and function,
which returns to the root-source of the mind— the stage of the five wisdoms of Vairocana Buddha.
The fundamental nature is the true suchness of the dharma-realm treasury;
entering the indestructible diamond nature,
one realizes the stage of noble wisdom and enlightenment, swiftly attaining the fruit of Buddhahood.
At that time, Vairocana Buddha spoke,
thus explaining how all Buddhas and all Bodhisattvas of the past, present, and future have studied, are studying, and will study [this].
Therefore, you and all the great assembly of bodhisattvas should contemplate and practice this well.
For hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, I have [cultivated this].
By practicing this mind, one enters the secret treasury of the Vajra Three Mysteries— the samādhi of the Buddhas—
and attains the fruit of Buddhahood, awakening to bodhi;
this serves as the cause.
At the outset, having abandoned the state of an ordinary being and attained equal and perfect enlightenment,
I am named Vairocana; I establish myself as the fundamental source for all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni wielded and expounded the five kinds of vajra-wisdom— the profound Great Dharma and Great Meaning of all Buddhas—
within the mind-nature of all sentient beings.
What do you think? Such as these— all Buddhas and all Bodhisattvas—
are identical with the World-Honored One Vairocana and the five wisdoms of the five Tathāgatas.
Together we shall practice and guide all sentient beings;
for the sake of all living creatures,
we have cultivated the path to Bodhi since our time on the causal ground.
At that time, they attained Buddhahood together under the name Thousand Śākyamunis,
along with the hundreds of thousands of millions of manifested Śākyamunis;
Vairocana dwelt together with them in the Lotus-womb World-Ocean.
That platform is surrounded by a thousand petals;
each petal is one world, thus constituting a thousand worlds.
I, Vairocana, have now manifested and transformed them into a thousand Śākyamunis for the sake of liberating and transforming sentient beings.
Following the thousandfold world system, there is a single-leaf world system,
which further contains ten billion Mount Sumerus, ten billion suns and moons,
ten billion sets of four continents, and ten billion Jambudvīpas in the south.
There are ten billion bodhisattvas and ten billion thrones for Śākyamuni;
the Buddha sits beneath ten billion bodhi trees,
each preaching the dharma concerning the bodhisattva you have questioned.
The "Chapter on the Practice of the Bodhisattva’s Mind-Ground Dharma" is thus;
it is likewise for each of the remaining nine hundred and ninety-nine Śākyamunis,
who each transform and deliver others by manifesting hundreds of thousands of millions of Śākyamunis.
At that time, Vairocana Buddha said:
"The Buddhas upon the thousand petals are my own emanations of the vajra-nature, the sacred wisdom of Dharma;
they are the hundreds of thousands of millions of Śākyamunis."
This is precisely the emanation-body of the thousand Śākyamunis; I am its source,
named the body of Vairocana Buddha.
Because it serves as the basis for the Dharma-treasury of Bodhi— the Great Wisdom of the Adamantine True Suchness— accomplished together with all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas,
at that time, Vairocana Tathāgata was upon the adamantine seat of the Lotus-womb Treasury.
He addressed Śākyamuni, the World-Honored One, saying:
"I shall provide a comprehensive response for the thousand Śākyas and the manifested hundreds of billions of Śākyas,
explaining how to practice the Mind-Ground when acting as a Bodhisattva."
Regarding that which you previously asked— the seed of the noble nature of bodhi and the noble wisdom of all vajras—
from the time when they were first on the stage of the causal ground,
all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas...
Since how many eons have I practiced and entered the path to Buddhahood?
For myself and all sentient beings, I shall open the Dharma-gate of the Ground of Mind and lead them into the Bodhi-path of Vajra-wisdom.
By means of the power of the noble ones, the noble wisdom,
and the noble nature, they empower the noble wisdom of the fundamental nature within the mental ground of all sentient beings who are training as bodhisattvas.
One swiftly reaches the fundamental source, the naturally pure *dharmakāya* and *jñānakāya*,
the stage of a Tathāgata of Vajra-Bodhi;
having attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, one is fully perfected.
Therefore, at that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata again questioned Vairocana Vajrasattva regarding the three secrets of the mind-ground and the threefold awakening;
then Śākyamuni Buddha spoke:
He also addressed the thousands of millions of emanated Śākyamunis:
"I now again petition the World-Honored One Vairocana to once more proclaim the fundamental secret Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas."
It expounds the treasury of all Bodhisattva teachings;
it expounds the treasury of the Dharma and Vinaya teachings of all Śrāvakas;
and it expounds the treasury of wisdom for all Mahābrahmā deities practicing the Bodhisattva path.
This is the teaching on the Dharma-gate of the Mind-Ground of all sentient beings,
the ocean-treasury of the self-nature of the Buddha-nature of the three mysteries of bodhi.
It is for all such Bodhisattvas and all sentient beings who practice according to these teachings.
By what causes and by what conditions does one attain entry into these forty-two bodhisattva stages of holy realization, and enter the stages of the holy ground,
the vajra-bodhi, the stage of equal enlightenment, and the stage of wondrous enlightenment?
If one attains it, what will the fruit of Buddhahood be like?
First, the Bodhisattva should practice and enter the Vajra,
the five patiences, suchness, the limit of reality, and the original source.
The Buddha-way of the noble wisdom of the suchness of intrinsic nature.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni shall immediately give rise to the noble intention.
Vajrapāṇi addressed Vairocana Tathāgata, saying:
"If a bodhisattva cultivates and studies the seed of the fundamental vajra-bodhi-sacred wisdom-nature,
causing it to enter the samādhi of the Buddha’s sacred nature..."
"What do you think?
At that time, the Tathāgata Vairocana addressed Śākyamuni, saying:"
If there are any bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who,
for the sake of all sentient beings,
seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, [they should...]
A bodhisattva training in awakening does not spare body or life;
they should relinquish all else and seek unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening,
first delivering all sentient beings.
Those who shall swiftly attain Buddhahood and realize Bodhi do so because these bodhisattvas rely upon the power of the Tathāgata’s great vows,
thereby accomplishing all vajra-liberations.
Then one shall be identical to the adamantine sacred ground of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas,
for one abides in the Bodhi of the Buddhas.
At that time, within the Great Assembly of the Dharma-realm in the Lotus-womb Treasury of the Ocean of Adamantine Nature, [one attains realization].
Within that assembly of all bodhisattvas,
there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva of great wisdom and supernormal powers who rose from his seat,
prostrated with his head at the feet [of the Buddha], and joined his palms in reverence.
Now, before the presence of Vairocana Tathāgata, I again most earnestly make this great vow:
may my mind be equal to space and as firm as a vajra,
so that I may attain non-retrogressive bodhi.
I shall practice the stages of cultivation in succession through the forty-two levels to extensively deliver sentient beings.
If space were to be exhausted, then the deliverance of sentient beings would cease;
but since space is inexhaustible, my deliverance of sentient beings shall likewise never come to rest.
When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Great Wisdom-Penetration had made this great vow,
at that moment, from within the Lotus-Ocean-Treasury of the Dharma Realm,
there suddenly emerged as many great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges multiplied by the number of atoms in a mote of dust, appearing to bear witness.
At that time, all the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas said:
"Now, through the profound penetration and empowerment of the Tathāgata’s holy nature,
we have simultaneously seen and heard the Bodhisattva Mahāprajñā."
Once they had made these vast and far-reaching vows,
all the Buddhas appeared and acted as witnesses;
therefore, the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas spoke.
"We, too, shall rejoice, for we all share the same vow as the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Great Wisdom-Penetration (Mahājñānābhijña).
Our minds are equal to space as we extensively deliver sentient beings without ceasing. At that time, there were all the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, as numerous as atoms.
Then those who possess the same wisdom as the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and extensively practice the bodhisattva path should make this great vow:
"May we study and practice until the end of the future,
aspiring with resolve to seek unexcelled bodhi without ever regressing."
Within the forty-two stages of the Dharma-gates,
one practices and studies in successive order;
from the stage of firm faith and forbearance, one enters the ten minds of initial departure.
The Vajra Samādhi of the Thirty-Branch Contemplation Gate of the Secrets of All Buddhas is now indicated as the orientation toward the fruit of Bodhi;
it begins from the stage of practicing the ten levels of faith.
How does one cultivate the entry into the ten stages of the path of departure?
First is the mind of relinquishment:
relinquishing all things as well as one's own body.
First, the mind of renunciation: relinquishing one's kingdom, city, wife, and children entirely.
Second, the mind of ethical discipline:
upholding the ten inexhaustible precepts of a bodhisattva.
And the Mahāyāna precepts of all Buddhas.
Third is the mind of patience,
within the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Fourth is the mind of exertion:
practicing all the wholesome dharmas of the Tathāgata with constant diligence.
Fifth is the concentrated mind,
which remains constantly in right concentration regarding all phenomena.
Sixth is the wise mind.
Sixth is skillful wisdom, which is capable of practicing with expertise regarding all Buddha-dharmas.
Seventh is the aspirational mind,
which gives rise to a vast heart of great compassion toward all phenomena.
May I rescue and deliver all sentient beings.
Eighth is the protection of the mind:
regarding all the Buddha-dharmas.
They constantly give rise to the bodhisattva’s great mind that protects the Dharma.
Ninth is the mind of joy,
which brings peace and happiness to all sentient beings.
One should constantly give rise to a mind of joy and bliss.
Tenth is the "crown-of-the-head" mind:
like the crown of a person's head, which is high and noble and cannot be seen.
Contemplating the mind in right concentration is the most supreme among all Buddhist teachings;
it is called the "Crown of Contemplative Illumination.
Since the mind is its very essence, it is termed the Bodhisattva’s cultivation of entry into the ten stages of development (*daśa-vyākaraṇa-citta*) directed toward the fruit.
At that time, the Tathāgata Vairocana, the source and essence of suchness,
addressed all the Buddhas, saying:
"You should know that from the first moment of generating the mind of enlightenment, a bodhisattva aspires with firm conviction."
From the stage of firm faith and patience, one enters the ten minds of progression (*daśa-prasthāna-citta*).
Entering into the practice of firm dharma-patience (*dharmanidhyāna-kṣānti*), one cultivates the ten minds of nourishment (*daśa-poṣaṇa-citta*).
Thus, through training in the bodhicitta, one is directed toward the fruit.
First is the mind of loving-kindness (*maitrī-citta*);
loving-kindness is able to bestow happiness.
Second is the mind of compassion (*karuṇā-citta*).
Compassion (*karuṇā*) is able to uproot suffering.
Third is the mind of joy (*muditā*):
because one realizes that the nature of phenomena is unborn, the path of bodhi-wisdom gives rise to a heart of joy.
Fourth is the mind of relinquishment (*upekṣā-citta*).
It consists of relinquishing all conditioned things,
as well as relinquishing everything— including kingdoms, cities, one's own body, wife, children, sons, and daughters.
Fifth is the mind of giving:
to give away all conditioned things— body and life, sons and daughters,
wife and children, as well as internal and external possessions— and the mind itself.
One gives away kingdoms, cities, fields, and houses— indeed, everything entirely.
Sixth is the mind of kind speech,
which bestows both others and oneself upon them.
Seventh is the beneficial mind (*anugrāhaka-citta*),
because one constantly maintains a benevolent intention and speaks kindly toward all people in all internal and external circumstances.
The bodhisattva takes upon himself their misdeeds because his mind of benefiting is constantly and eternally dedicated to providing aid to all sentient beings.
Eighth is the shared mind.
Together with all sentient beings,
one enters equally into the mind of non-arising and enters equally into the dharmas of bodhi;
this is called the samādhi of shared dharma, because one attains a single-mindedness [with others].
Ninth is the concentrated mind.
This is because one attains the right view, right nature, and right concentration of all Tathāgatas, as well as the wisdom of all Buddhas,
through the accomplishment of bodhi by means of the power of meditative concentration and the mind of samādhi.
Tenth is the mind of wisdom (*prajñā-citta*).
Because it is able to give rise to all Buddha-dharmas and the *prajñāpāramitā* within all wisdom, it is called the mind of wisdom.
This is called the Bodhisattva’s cultivation and study of the ten nurturing minds directed toward the fruit of Bodhi.
Therefore, the Tathāgata Vairocana, whose body is the holy wisdom of the Vajra, declared:
All Buddhas should know that all these bodhisattvas,
from within the practice of the endurance of the firm dharma (*dharmakṣānti*),
cultivate the ten ways of nurturing the mind and enter into the firm cultivation of endurance.
Practice the ten adamantine minds and train in the bodhicitta directed toward the fruition.
First is profound faith.
Regarding the profound Dharma-treasury of the Mahāyāna of all Buddhas,
one constantly practices great faith and never regresses;
this is called "great and profound faith."
Second is the mind of mindfulness.
It consists of not losing the correct wisdom of all Buddhas through mindfulness,
and maintaining the mind of precepts, concentration, and wisdom regarding the profound and subtle meaning of the Mahāyāna.
This is called the mind of mindfulness.
Third is the mind of dedication,
which dedicates [merit] toward the Mahāyāna teachings and the unsurpassed, perfectly complete, vajra-like bodhi of the Tathāgatas.
It is called the mind of dedication to the Mahāyāna.
Fourth is the mind of penetration,
which penetrates the principle of the Tathāgata’s noble wisdom.
Because the mind that realizes and illuminates quiescence, being pure both internally and externally, is called the "mind of realization," this is the fifth:
the direct mind (*ṛju-citta*).
It is the nature of the mind of right wisdom on the straight, correct, and holy path.
Being upright, without crookedness, without false views or flattery,
and because the true nature of ultimate emptiness is called the "straight mind," this is the sixth:
the non-regressive mind.
It is called the mind that strives for enlightenment because it never regresses;
it is called the non-regressive mind because its nature is realized as unchanging.
Seventh is the Mahāyāna mind.
Because it does not enter the two vehicles nor the various evil attachments and views of external paths,
it is called the Mahāyāna mind.
Eighth is the signless mind.
It does not enter into any characteristics of conditioned phenomena,
nor does it enter into the forms and images of the five sensory objects;
this is called the unconditioned and signless mind.
Ninth is the mind of wisdom.
Because it is unimpeded regarding all the wisdom of all Buddhas,
it is called the mind of wisdom.
Tenth is the indestructible mind.
Because one does not destroy the Mahāyāna right view, the right wisdom of bodhi, and the Buddha-mind—
this is called the indestructible Mahāyāna mind.
This is called the Bodhisattva’s sequential cultivation of the ten adamantine minds directed toward the fruit of bodhi.
At that time, the Tathāgata Vairocana of the Noble Nature-Body addressed [him], saying:
All Buddhas, you should know that from within the firm cultivation of the practice of patience,
a bodhisattva cultivates the ten adamantine minds.
Entering into the steadfast noble patience,
one cultivates the path toward the ten noble stages and proceeds toward the fruition of the bodhicitta.
First is the Ground of the Equality of Essential Nature;
second is the Ground of the Good Wisdom of Essential Nature;
third is the Ground of the Radiance of Essential Nature.
Fourth is the stage of the essential nature of objective phenomena (jñeya);
fifth is the stage of the essential nature of wisdom-illumination;
sixth is the stage of the essential nature of radiant flowers.
Seventh is the Stage of Fulfillment of Essential Nature;
eighth is the Stage of the Buddha’s Lion’s Roar of Essential Nature;
ninth is the Stage of the Flower Ornament of Essential Nature.
Tenth is the entry into the Buddha-ground through the essential nature.
Therefore, at that time, it is called the tenth stage of the noble Bodhisattvas, wherein one cultivates the aspiration for enlightenment directed toward its fruition.
At that moment, the Dharmakāya Vairocana Tathāgata addressed them, saying:
All Buddhas should know this:
from the ten adamantine minds, the bodhisattva enters into the firm and holy patience;
by cultivating the ten holy stages, they enter the stage of the Buddha-Tathāgata.
Cultivating the bodhicitta directed toward the fruit of Buddhahood:
first, the measure of the stage of equal enlightenment through the samādhi of vajra-wisdom;
in its dharmas, it is equal and identical to that of the Tathāgata.
The essence, the limit of reality, and the single nature of all phenomena as suchness is called the Stage of Perfect Enlightenment (Samyaksambuddha-bhūmi).
Second is the Stage of Wondrous Enlightenment (Pratyekabuddha-bhūmi).
Through the power of hundreds of thousands of billions of subtle, sublime, noble wisdoms and vajra-intelligence,
they enter the stage of wondrous enlightenment, the Vajropama-samādhi,
and cultivate their entry into this stage.
Because one has accomplished the Tathāgata’s liberation and the great wisdom-body of the Vajra-prajñāpāramitā, thereby fulfilling the Dharma-body,
it is called the Holy Nature, the Stage of Sublime Enlightenment.
Therefore, they are called all Buddhas,
for they have cultivated entry into the Tathāgata’s adamantine stage of wondrous enlightenment and have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, Vairocana, acting as the manifest embodiment of the Five Wisdom Tathāgatas, together proclaimed the Dharma-gate of the Treasury of the Forty-two Stages, the Vajra Wisdom of Prajñā, which is the equality of the dharma-body nature of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
Vairocana said:
"Together with me and the five Tathāgatas,
all Buddhas, and all Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas."
Since the distant past of former lives on the causal ground,
while practicing as a bodhisattva, he has extensively cultivated the bodhisattva path and cultivated the root source for entering the fruit of Buddhahood, which is bodhi.
In this way, all bodhisattvas and all sentient beings together cultivate and enter these ten stages of departure, ten stages of nurturing, ten adamantine stages,
the holy path of the ten bhūmis, the stage of the nature of perfect enlightenment, and the stage of wondrously enlightened Buddhahood.
Because when one attains the fruit of Buddhahood— the unsurpassed, perfect,
and complete enlightenment— it is the unconditioned, signless, great, fulfilled, pure, and eternally abiding Dharma-body; therefore,
the Tathāgata has said that it should be explained in its proper sequence.
At that time, the World-Honored One Vairocana proceeded to expound the eighth chapter.
The eighth is the eighth chapter on the sequential cultivation and dedication toward Bodhi for the three classes of worthy bodhisattvas as they enter the stages of the Dharma.

At that time, Vairocana Tathāgata, the Honored One of the Five Wisdoms, the Holy Nature of Vajra, within the Dharma-Ocean Lotus-Womb World, abided in the Samādhi of the Pure Vajra-Wisdom-Nature and the Dharma-Treasury of the Maṇi-Jewel-Nature. Within this Dharma-treasury of the Samādhi of the Vajra-Nature Ocean, Vairocana Tathāgata—
He manifested a thousand billion Śākyamunis and a thousand billion great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
At that time, within this assembly of bodhisattvas,
there was a bodhisattva named Mahājñānābhijña (Great Wisdom Supernatural Power).
Arising from the Samādhi of the King of a Thousand Lights,
he again addressed Vairocana, saying:
"World-Honored One, as the Tathāgata has previously stated."
A brief exposition of the secret dharma-gate of the path of the mind-ground:
the characteristics of the ten stages of setting forth, the ten stages of nurturing, the ten vajra stages,
and the stages of Equal Enlightenment, Wondrous Enlightenment, and Buddhahood.
Within each and every one of these meanings, there is still that which cannot yet be understood.
I pray that you will explain it;
I pray that you will explain it—the Dharma-treasury of the nature of reality, the gate of omniscience, the samādhi of the supreme, ultimate, vajra-like holy nature and holy power.
The samādhi-gates of all Buddhas,
the gates of all samādhis,
and the gates of all vajras.
The gateways of all dhāraṇīs;
the gateways of mastery in all supernatural powers;
and the gateways of all space.
Regarding the gate of all unconditioned non-characteristics and the gate of all doors of liberation,
the Bodhisattva Mahājñānābhijña questioned the Tathāgata.
"Therefore, how should a bodhisattva practice and how should they train so as to realize this dharma-gate and achieve awakening?
At that time, the Tathāgata Vairocana replied:
The Thousand Buddhas, as well as all the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāprajñā-Abhijñā Bodhisattvas, and others, should know this.
The Buddha said: "Good sons, listen attentively, listen attentively!
As for the meaning of that which you previously asked:"

By practicing the gate of contemplation, one enters the ten stages of the aspiring mind (*citta-prasthāna*), the ten stages of the nurturing mind (*citta-vardhana*), the ten adamantine minds (*vajra-citta*), and the ten noble grounds (*ārya-bhūmi*), as well as the two sublime stages (*viśeṣa-bhūmi*).
This proceeds sequentially from the beginning within the holy path of the Buddha-ground of the mind.
"How should one practice to enter this Dharma-door and attain Bodhi?
The Buddha addressed the great Bodhisattvas, those of great wisdom and supernatural powers, saying: "I shall now analyze and explain it for you."
First, from within the stage of firm faith and forbearance (*kṣānti*),
one cultivates entry into the ten minds of departure (*daśa-prasthāna-citta*) directed toward the fruit of Bodhi.
At that time, the Tathāgata Vairocana...
I shall now, for the sake of the assembly, uphold and proclaim the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*).
This subtle and profound teaching shall be revealed once more;
first, I will set forth the gate of contemplation for entering the ten stages of faith (*daśa-śraddhā*) as the preliminary to realization and cultivation.
One enters the sequential cultivation from the very first arising.
First is the mind of equanimity (*upekṣā-citta*).
If a bodhisattva, regarding all things, maintains a mind of equanimity...
Practicing the perfection of the pāramitā of giving,
they give rise to vast vows and practices while traversing the bodhisattva path;
they cultivate and maintain the ten pāramitās and all profound noble practices.
First, they relinquish all wealth, food, drink, and medicinal decoctions,
constantly and perpetually making offerings to the Buddhas and the Triple Gem;
their minds are free from hoarding, without priority or sequence.
Gradually practicing superior conduct,
he will later become a sovereign king who renounces his kingdom, lands, and cities, no longer acting as their ruler.
If one would destroy stinginess and greed, one should likewise relinquish fields, houses, gold, and silver.
The bright pearl does not harbor the thought of being a precious treasure.
Next, one should relinquish sons, daughters, male and female slaves, carriages, horses, wife, children,
and even one's own body, never allowing desire or attachment to dwell in the mind.
Regarding all conditioned phenomena and all precious material wealth—
since all such things must be relinquished— one should,
at that time, proceed sequentially toward one's own body and mind.
Grasping at views and the conceit of self,
they falsely assemble and establish the designation of a "master.
They construct the view of a self, thereby giving rise to all forms of attachment and bondage.
Furthermore, there are the twelve links of dependent origination,
which neither combine nor disperse, have no substance, and involve neither abandonment nor reception.
One should practice by relinquishing all things, giving rise to the unconditioned mind and the signless mind.
By means of the contemplation of non-arising and emptiness, one enters the right concentration of the mind.
One eliminates the twelve bases, the eighteen elements, the five aggregates, the six sense organs, and the six sense objects,
unifying all phenomena into a single integrated whole.
They are fully able to pacify and extinguish [all things], attaining non-self and the absence of "mine.
All phenomena are formed through the provisional combination of the characteristic of emptiness—
whether they be all internal phenomena or all external phenomena.
Within the true nature of all mundane and supramundane phenomena,
there is neither relinquishing nor grasping;
therefore, a bodhisattva should always practice total relinquishment, as if it were the nature of space.
At this time, it is called a provisional assembly formed by the synthesis of illusions;
because the purity of the nature of observation manifests before one,
one abandons the mind and enters the nature to realize the Samādhi of Emptiness.
The second is the mind of ethical discipline (*śīla-citta*).
If there is a bodhisattva who is able to uphold the Mahāyāna precepts of the Tathāgata,
it is for the sake of all sentient beings as well as for one's own person.
One who can uphold the ten inexhaustible precepts of a Mahāyāna bodhisattva is able,
both for themselves and for all others, to constantly perceive the nature of the mind and the nature of the precepts as being like space.
To hold [to precepts] is to be deluded and inverted.
Within the fundamental self-nature of their own root,
Bodhisattvas perceive no precepts within pure *tathatā*.
This means that the nature of precepts is like space, and one does not perceive the precepts of others.
Within the mind-nature of a bodhisattva who maintains the precepts,
the precepts are neither precepts nor non-precepts, and there is no recipient.
The ten wholesome precepts, the teacherless Dharma-precepts, and even all instances of deception,
theft, greed, anger, and wrong views—
none of these have a gatherer, nor do they have a disperser.
Because there is neither the receiving of precepts nor the non-receiving of precepts,
the nature of the Noble Path is entirely pure;
the nature of the path of upholding the precepts is likewise so.
A bodhisattva should always maintain pure prohibitive precepts while practicing the bodhisattva path;
they should always share the same mind, the same nature, the same conduct, and the same virtue as all sentient beings.
Constantly practicing kindness, goodness, purity, uprightness, truthfulness, and right view;
abandoning anger and delighting in all virtues and non-virtues with equanimity—
this is called maintaining the ten major heavy precepts of right nature.
This is also the bodhisattva’s maintenance of the essential nature of the ten inexhaustible precepts;
it restrains the eight inversions and,
regarding the nature of all sages, consists of the mind of meditative concentration that is free from conceptual illumination.
Because true stillness manifests as a single path of purity;
third is the mind of patience.
One who attains this patience [realizes it] within the fundamental source-nature of all sentient beings.
The absence of any characteristic of patience is called the patience of signless wisdom.
Within this signless nature of patience and wisdom,
the bodhisattva causes their wisdom to be able to illuminate the essence of the mind.
Realizing the self-nature of the essence, one attains purity of mind;
realizing that this pure nature is devoid of substantiality and penetrating into universal emptiness is called the "patience of emptiness" (śūnyatā-kṣānti).
If a bodhisattva is able to practice the conduct of universal vows and patience toward all sentient beings,
it is called patience in all circumstances.
In all forms of patience, the bodhisattva enters the patience of non-arising;
they constantly observe that the fundamental nature of their own body’s activity is neither born nor extinguished.
Having realized the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*),

the Bodhisattva, in the course of his practice, should further cultivate the three kinds of great patience for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

If one is slandered or harmed by others, one does not give rise to thoughts of resentment, but practices the patience of enduring enmity while performing the bodhisattva conduct toward the entire realm of sentient beings,
even when constantly subjected to such treatment by others.
When afflictions and obstacles arise, one does not give rise to suffering or distress;
rather, one establishes the minds of oneself and all sentient beings in purity.
This entry into the mind of pure nature is called the patience of accepting suffering.
In all objective spheres, the bodhisattva practices immeasurable vows and maintains a mind of immeasurable patience within each and every practice.
To contemplate thoroughly the nature of formations so as to realize the nature of the mind is called the "patience of discerning phenomena" (*dharmānupaśyanākṣānti*).
Among all forms of patience, it is included within the three types of patience regarding phenomena.
Not perceiving any patience is called the bodhisattva’s patience of signless practice.
Next, within the nature of the patience of signless practice,
the bodhisattva employs the contemplation of the patience of signless practice as being devoid of the characteristic of a recipient.
There is no thought of striking, no thought of weapons or staves,
no thought of killing or harming, and no thought of malice;
all are entirely the nature of suchness, devoid of any arising characteristic.
Within the pure essence of the noble nature of the bodhisattva’s mind,
there is neither one nor two;
it is a single truth and a single illumination.
Contemplate the single nature and single characteristic:
there is no non-existence, yet there is the characteristic of non-existence;
it is not the characteristic of non-mind, yet it is the characteristic of being conditioned by non-conditioning.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining; in movement or stillness;
regarding self, person, a sovereign, bondage, or liberation—one clearly and distinctly perceives that all phenomena are entirely without marks.
One perceives that the nature of phenomena is empty and quiescent;
the nature of being without self-nature, the suchness of the noble path, and all emptiness are likewise thus.
This is because the characteristic of patience and the nature of emptiness are both unapprehendable.
All bodhisattvas should be diligent in their resolve to cultivate and study all dharmas, patience, signlessness, and the noble path.
Fourth is the advancement of the mind.
In the four modes of deportment,
the bodhisattva constantly practices the great compassionate vows and conduct of a mahāsattva,
seeking Mahāyāna bodhi for the sake of all sentient beings.
One should always practice diligence so that self-benefit and the benefit of others are never in vain.
Within the four modes of conduct— walking, standing,
sitting, and reclining— a bodhisattva should constantly contemplate the nature of the mind through wisdom.
At all times, they constantly enter the noble wisdom-samādhi of the emptiness of phenomena,
illuminating the noble nature of the mind.
The nature is pure, yet it is a provisional union and a provisional assembly;
one perceives the quiescence within the dharma-nature of the mind,
ascends the mountain of non-arising, and enters the path of the unconditioned.
One perceives the nature of all internal and external phenomena;
the nature of all dharmas is empty, void, and non-existent.
Whether existent or non-existent, they are empty in their nature as the four great elements.
All forms and appearances are likewise like space.
Regarding external conditioned objects,
all forms— whether blue, yellow, red, white, or any other color— are also thus.
Because their nature is identical to emptiness,
the bodhisattva penetrates emptiness and does not perceive any form as having the characteristics of the conditioned.
